title: Drawing Telephone: meaningful two-player relay
content: Instructor: Codex. Version recorded in the completion receipt. The owner found the old two-player mode confusing: the person who wrote the original prompt was asked to guess that same prompt after their partner drew it. A two-person chain cannot create an unknown final guess with player-authored prompts, so the game now provides a private surprise scene to a drawer, asks the other player to guess the drawing, reveals both, and swaps roles. Quick has two sketches and Standard four. The 3–8-player Telephone chain is retained.
architecture: app/games-telephone.mjs owns deterministic round rules and action-log save recovery; a variant field separates the two-player duo relay from the 3–8-player chain and restores older two-player saves as legacy games. app/games-telephone-ui.mjs presents covered handoffs, a private prompt to the drawer, a drawing-only guess view, full reveals and bilingual setup instructions. app/sw.js advances the offline shell cache. Existing games and saves are preserved.
techniques: Derive round counts and stage kinds from the variant, never from the player count alone after a save. Keep the secret prompt outside contributions until the reveal, while showing it only on the active drawer screen. Replay actions to validate saves. Use real browser pointer strokes and page reloads to test the whole handoff. Test both languages, menu language switches, five viewports and a stopped-server offline completion.
mistakes: The first prototype sent player one back to guess their own authored prompt. Changing only menu copy would leave a meaningless game; the reducer and end-to-end paths needed distinct duo rules. A browser check assumed three name inputs after merely changing the player-count select; triggering its change event fixed the test setup. Existing two-player saves could break if reinterpreted under new rules, so absence of a variant replays the legacy flow. The broad gate exposed unrelated baseline and timing failures: screen prose was mistaken for a command, recall tests captured yesterday before midnight, and the skill smoke scanned live processes until its 20-second timeout. These received narrow safety and test-isolation fixes. Human playtesting is still needed for fun and native-speaker review for Kreyòl.
dependencies: Existing Playhouse ES modules, service worker, Node and Edge CDP harness. The game adds no dependencies, paid APIs or network service.
exercises: Run node tests/node/test_playhouse_telephone.mjs, node scripts/playhouse_browser_check.mjs and node scripts/playhouse_offline_browser.mjs. Run scripts.development_task with docs/playhouse-mystery-checks.json to record all checks. Inspect data/playhouse-evidence/telephone-duo-mobile.png and the browser/offline result JSON. On one phone with two people, start a new Quick game, keep the drawer's prompt private, then each draw and guess once. Record actual minutes, confusion, peeks and whether they want a rematch.
